userPrompt:
The planning prompt that a story's draft run is sent with (planning.pi, listed in spec/scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.pi#BakedSystemPrompts.prompts) asks the run to judge whether the story holds one piece of work or several.

If it holds several, the run should propose:
- the story's rewrite, `target: rewrite`, as the first piece, with that piece's steps (target: the story's id)
- a `target: new` block for each other piece, each with its own title, mode, spec citations, and prompt

Each block follows the form spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.proposals describes. The prompt should tell the run not to split one piece of work into several stories just to make them smaller: steps are for pieces of one story, and new stories are for separate work. Its worked example should show a split.

Update the planning.pi line in spec/scope/harness-integration/baked-prompts/index.pi#BakedSystemPrompts.prompts to say this too. Then rebuild so that system-prompts/compiled.json carries the new prompt.

Don't re-read anything you've already read.

The prompt the chain was sent:

"Draft with agent" (and "Ask agent" on an open story) can turn one rough story into several stories, not just one full story.

Today, spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.draftingWithAgent asks each run only to "turn it into a full story": a rewrite plus its steps. Change it so that when a rough story holds more than one piece of work, the run proposes:
- the rewrite of the story itself, as the first piece, with its steps
- a "New story" proposal for each other piece, each with its own title, prompt, mode, and spec citations, grounded as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.specGrounding says

A story that is one piece of work still gets just its rewrite and steps, as before.

Once this is done, all of the following should be true:
- The card's proposal count ("3 proposals") counts the new stories along with the rewrite and the additions.
- The open story's "Proposals" list shows them all, in the order given. The rewrite comes first, then the new stories and the additions in the order the run gave them.
- Each new story's card reads "New story", as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.proposalCards labels it.
- Accepting a new story puts it at the end of the Backlog, marked "From agent", as now. It never goes into Draft (spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.description) and never into Next sprint.
- Accepting a new story split off a Draft story does not move that story. Only accepting its rewrite or one of its additions moves it to the Backlog, as spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.draftingWithAgent says.
- "Accept all" accepts the rewrite and every new story together.

spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.proposals already allows a "New story" target. The spec has nothing yet on splitting one story into several, so that part is new. Update spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.draftingWithAgent and spec/scope/planning/index.pi#Planning.drafting to say it, then make the application handle new-story proposals from a story's draft run as described above.

What the spec step said it changed, its final output:

A "Draft with agent" or "Ask agent" run is now asked to split a story that holds more than one piece of work. I couldn't compile or run the tests: this sandbox blocks reading `.suspense/system-prompts/*.md`, which the crate pulls in at build time. So the changes have only been checked by reading them.

- **The draft prompt:** I added a `split` piece to `system-prompts/planning.pi`. The rebuilt `compiled.json` already contains it. It asks for the story's rewrite first, with its steps, then a `target: new` story for each other piece, each with its own title, prompt, mode and grounded citations. A story that is one piece of work still gets only its rewrite and steps. `draft_request` in `src/planning.rs` adds this text whenever the draft is about a story, so it covers both entry points.
- **Order:** when a run ends, its proposals are stable-sorted so the rewrite comes first. The new stories and additions keep the order the run gave them, after any proposals already waiting.
- **Already true before this change:** the card count includes every kind of proposal, and a new story's card reads "New story". Accepting one puts it at the end of the Backlog marked "From agent". Only accepting a rewrite or an addition moves a Draft story. "Accept all" accepts everything waiting.

I added a test, `a_draft_splits_its_story_into_new_stories`, covering the order, the count, where an accepted new story goes, the Draft story staying put, and "Accept all". It needs a build with access to those prompt files before it can run. The spec and the prompt agreed, so there was nothing to reconcile.
